text:
maria: Quick proposal — instead of carving static per-endpoint burst pools (chat vs embeddings vs streaming), what if we do a weighted-routing + adaptive-smoothing layer so endpoints get priority slices but can borrow during idle periods?

sam: curious, can you sketch how the weights vs borrowing work?

maria: yeah. idea: each endpoint has a weight (w_chat, w_embed, w_rerank, w_stream). Normal steady-state capacity = total_tokens * w_x / sum(w). Bursts allowed up to borrow_limit = alpha * idle_capacity from other endpoints. Smoothing window uses EWMA of token rate to avoid immediate overcommit.

leo: sounds promising. how do we enforce quotas for keys/orgs? per-key token-bucket + admission that respects weighted share?

maria: exactly — admission checks two buckets: 1) key/org bucket (hard limit) 2) endpoint-weighted pool token account (softly enforced with smoothing). If endpoint wants > pool, it can borrow if other endpoints are underutilized and borrowing <= borrow_limit.

jess: UX-wise, console should show: current weight, effective capacity, borrowed_in, borrowed_out, and a small sparkline of EWMA rate. Also an explanation tool-tip: "why did my chat call get 429 while embeddings didn't?"

sam: edgecases: streaming connections keep tokens flowing slowly but hold sockets — could starve chat's short high-burst calls. we should treat streaming weight as "long-lived" and cap concurrent inflight streams separately.

maria: agreed. separate limiter for concurrent streams + token weight. streaming can borrow token-cap but not concurrency.

leo: what about failover? if borrow_limit reached, route to cheaper model or enqueue? we need fallback policy chain.

maria: fallback chain: same-model-degraded-> compatible-smaller-quantized -> enqueue for short delay -> 429. Policy order configurable per org. console shows active policy.

jess: can we show this in the rollout UX? like enable weighted-routing as a gradual flag with % exposure so we can watch per-org impact before turning on globally.

maria: yes — rollout plan: feature flag + canary cohort (10 orgs), monitor metrics: p50 latency, p95 latency, 429 rate by endpoint, borrow_rate, borrowed_tokens, and quality regressions for fallback routes.

sam: metrics wire-framing: suggest tags: endpoint, org_id, key_id, route_variant, borrow_direction. tracing for request path (admitted->borrowed_from->served_by).

leo: performance: admission check needs to be cheap. do it in a single atomic read-modify-write against shardable counters (approximate using sharded leaky buckets). avoid cross-shard sync on the hot path.

maria: yep — implement weighted pool counts as sharded token counters with fast local reservations and background reconcile. smoothing EWMA also local per shard.

jess: console query examples for SRE / support: show org X borrow history: 
```
select timestamp, endpoint, borrow_in, borrow_out, token_rate_ewma
from routing_borrow_metrics
where org_id = 'org-123' and timestamp > now() - 1h
```

leo: nice. one more: telemetry for alerts — set alert when borrow_rate > 20% for 5m or when queued_enqueue_ratio > 0.2.

sam: question re billing: borrowed tokens still billed to org that consumed them, right? otherwise incentives bad.

maria: yes charged to consumer org; borrowing is purely capacity sharing not cross-billing. need to annotate billing events with route_variant and borrowed flag.

jess: UX hint: console should show an "expected throttle" estimate per route in the route config UI given current weights and historical traffic. helps customers tune weights.

ops-bot: deploy: canary rollout started for weighted-routing v1 -> cohort "canary-10" (10 orgs). Logs: ./deploys/weighted-routing/v1/2026-03-18.log

sam: thanks — I'll add admission read path PR and a design doc. mari, can you add the console mockups? I'll own the infra counters.

maria: on it. I'll post the mock images in #design when ready. :thumbsup:
